facts.text: ProjectAirSimEnv subclasses gym.Env and, in its constructor, connects a ProjectAirSimClient and constructs a World from the scene configuration.
ProjectAirSimEnv defines close() as client.disconnect(), while reset() and step() are NotImplementedError hooks for concrete environments.
The gym registry maps ProjectAirSimDroneLanding-v0 to ProjectAirSimDroneLandingEnv in projectairsim_dronelanding_env.
The drone-landing environment uses a 0.100 s delta/step time, chosen to be longer than the flight controller's 50 Hz (20 ms) minimum command duration.
The observation shape is (4,) for dx, dy, dz and dyaw, and the action shape is (3,) for V_north, V_east and V_down.
The observation space is Box(-math.inf, math.inf, shape=(4,)) and the action space is Box(-1.0, 1.0, shape=(3,)).
reset() loads the scene, creates a Drone, subscribes to its actual_pose and collision_info, enables API control and arms the vehicle.

step() is async: it calls the drone's move_by_velocity_async with the three action components, advances the simulated world by dt, awaits the move task and returns the legacy four-tuple (observation, reward, done, info).
move_by_velocity_async documents v_north, v_east and v_down as desired velocities in world NED axes in m/s.
get_observation returns the actor pose relative to the landing pad as dx, dy, dz and the actor yaw; get_reward returns the L2 distance between the goal and actor poses.
collision_callback stores the collision info and sets done, which is the only path in this environment that ends an episode.
The environment's own comment marks landing-success termination as an unfinished TODO, so the pinned episode ends on collision only.
The drone-landing scene uses a steppable clock with a 5,000,000 ns step that pauses on start.
World.continue_for_sim_time continues the simulation for delta_time_nanos and then pauses.
World.pause sends the scene's Pause service request with do_pause True.
World.is_paused sends the scene's IsPaused service request and returns its boolean answer.
The server's SimPause supports only a steppable clock, and ContinueForSimTime with wait_until_complete waits until the clock reports paused.
The client's service socket waits up to 300000 ms for a reply to each request.
request_async sends on a new socket context and returns an asyncio task that processes the reply.
disconnect stops the receive loop, joins the receive thread, unsubscribes and closes both sockets.
Inside the async step, the environment advances the world with the synchronous world.continue_for_sim_time call and only then awaits the move task.
World.continue_for_sim_time sends its ContinueForSimTime request through client.request.
client.request sends on the service socket and blocks in recv_msg until the reply arrives or the receive timeout expires.
The server's SimPause carries a TODO asking whether it should wait for external components such as Unreal to confirm the pause before returning.
The server's IsPaused service returns the simulation clock's paused flag.
The Linux client setup installs the Python client library from client/python/projectairsim with pip install -e.
The client's autonomy extra pins gym==0.18.3; the base dependencies do not include gym.

determinism.notes: The native reset takes no seed; the fake is deterministic analytic code, but no simulator or flight-controller determinism is claimed for either backend.

fidelity.engine: analytic:Python drone-landing stand-in (no Project AirSim server or Unreal)
gaps: the fake is an analytic kinematic stand-in: no dynamics, flight controller, sensors or collision detection; positions follow the commanded velocity directly
it keeps the native calling convention (coroutine step awaiting a command task, synchronous argument-free reset, world.pause/is_paused) but runs no Project AirSim client or Unreal scene
the upstream environment never sets done on a successful landing (its own TODO at line 85); the fake likewise keeps done false
camera, image and perception observations are not part of the selected base environment; only the 4-element pose/dyaw observation is exposed

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: The scene's steppable simulation clock reports paused (World.pause, read back by World.is_paused; Unreal is not asked to confirm) and no native step, reset or close is owned; a running continue_for_sim_time is not interrupted. Further step and reset are refused until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch.
